# Clipman
> Wayland-native clipboard history manager for GNOME on Linux, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. Press Super+V to search, pin and paste from a local SQLite-backed history. No telemetry; detected secrets are removed from the history.

- [Project page](https://mohammedel-sayedahmed.github.io/clipman/)
- [Source](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/clipman)
- [Design workspace](https://mohammedel-sayedahmed.github.io/clipman/design/index.html)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/clipman/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Features

- Wayland-native: a GNOME Shell extension reports copies over D-Bus; GNOME only for now (KDE and wlroots support is planned: issue #318)
- libadwaita UI: Adw.ApplicationWindow popup, sidebar Adw.Dialog settings (six panes), Adw.NavigationSplitView snippets editor, Catppuccin Mocha (dark) / warm-stone (light) palette overlay
- Privacy: incognito mode, detection of labelled passwords, tokens, keys and card numbers (removed from the history after 30 s), restrictive file permissions
- Search + pinning + reusable snippets with template variables (${date}, ${time}, ${clipboard})
- Open source, Apache-2.0, distributed on Snap Store / PyPI / AUR / .deb / .rpm

## Distribution

- Snap: `sudo snap install clipman`
- PyPI: `pipx install --system-site-packages clipman-clipboard` (the flag is required — the GTK4/libadwaita `gi` bindings are distro packages and cannot be pip-installed)
- AUR: `yay -S clipman-clipboard`
